398	-- Update (one of) callbacks registry for sqlite functions.
399	local function updatecb(self, where, name, f)
400	  local cbs = conncb[self][where]
401	  if cbs[name] then -- Callback already present, free old one.
402	    cbs[name]:free()
403	  end
404	  cbs[name] = f -- Could be nil and that's fine.
405	end

407	-- Return manually casted callback that sqlite expects, scalar.
408	local function scalarcb(name, f)
409	  local values = {} -- Conversion buffer.
410	  local function sqlf(context, nvalues, pvalues)
411	    -- Indexing 0,N-1.
412	    for i=1,nvalues do values[i] = get_value(pvalues[i - 1]) end
413	    -- Throw error via sqlite function if necessary.
414	    local ok, result = pcall(f, unpack(values, 1, nvalues))
415	    if not ok then
416	      local msg = "Lua registered scalar function "..name.." error: "..result
417	      sql.sqlite3_result_error(context, msg, #msg)
418	    else
419	      set_value(context, result)
420	    end
421	  end
422	  return ffi.cast("ljsqlite3_cbstep", sqlf)
423	end

425	-- Return the state for aggregate case (created via initstate()). We use the ptr
426	-- returned from aggregate_context() for tagging only, all the state data is
427	-- handled from Lua side.
428	local function getstate(context, initstate, size)
429	  -- Only pointer address relevant for indexing, size irrelevant.
430	  local ptr = sql.sqlite3_aggregate_context(context, size)
431	  local pid = tonumber(ffi.cast("intptr_t",ptr))
432	  local state = aggregatestate[pid]
433	  if type(state) == "nil" then
434	    state = initstate()
435	    aggregatestate[pid] = state
436	  end
437	  return state, pid
438	end

440	-- Return manually casted callback that sqlite expects, stepper for aggregate.
441	local function stepcb(name, f, initstate)
442	  local values = {} -- Conversion buffer.
443	  local function sqlf(context, nvalues, pvalues)
444	    -- Indexing 0,N-1.
445	    for i=1,nvalues do values[i] = get_value(pvalues[i - 1]) end
446	    local state = getstate(context, initstate, 1)
447	    -- Throw error via sqlite function if necessary.
448	    local ok, result = pcall(f, state, unpack(values, 1, nvalues))
449	    if not ok then
450	      local msg = "Lua registered step function "..name.." error: "..result
451	      sql.sqlite3_result_error(context, msg, #msg)
452	    end
453	  end
454	  return ffi.cast("ljsqlite3_cbstep", sqlf)
455	end

457	-- Return manually casted callback that sqlite expects, finalizer for aggregate.
458	local function finalcb(name, f, initstate)
459	  local function sqlf(context)
460	    local state, pid = getstate(context, initstate, 0)
461	    aggregatestate[pid] = nil -- Clear the state.
462	    local ok, result = pcall(f, state)
463	    -- Throw error via sqlite function if necessary.
464	    if not ok then
465	      local msg = "Lua registered final function "..name.." error: "..result
466	      sql.sqlite3_result_error(context, msg, #msg)
467	    else
468	      set_value(context, result)
469	    end
470	  end
471	  return ffi.cast("ljsqlite3_cbfinal", sqlf)
472	end

477	  local code = sql.sqlite3_create_function(self._ptr, name, -1, 5, nil,

484	  jit.off(stmt_step) -- Necessary to avoid bad calloc in some use cases.

528	stmt_step = function(self, row, header)
529	  -- Must check code ~= SQL_DONE or sqlite3_step --> undefined result.
530	  if self._code == sql.SQLITE_DONE then return nil end -- Already finished.
531	  self._code = sql.sqlite3_step(self._ptr)
532	  if self._code == sql.SQLITE_ROW then
533	    -- All the sql.* functions called never errors here.
534	    row = row or {}
535	    for i=1,self:_ncol() do
536	      row[i] = get_column(self._ptr, i - 1)
537	    end
538	    if header then self:_header(header) end
539	    return row, header
540	  elseif self._code == sql.SQLITE_DONE then -- Have finished now.
541	    return nil
542	  else -- If code not DONE or ROW then it's error.
543	    E_conn(self._conn, self._code)
544	  end
545	end
546	stmt_mt._step = stmt_step

-- Gkyl ------------------------------------------------------------------------
--
-- Jenkins helper: evaluate the MOAT regression results written by
-- 'gkeyll runregression run --moat check' and fail (os.exit(1)) if any test
-- did not pass, unless it's listed in the per-PR acknowledgment file.
--
-- Usage: gkeyll ci/jenkins/check_regression_results.lua <resultsDir> [ackFile]
--   <resultsDir>  the gkeyll-results/ directory written by 'runregression
--                 configure' (i.e. <prefix>/gkeyll-results).
--   [ackFile]     optional path to a text file listing "<layer>/<name>"
--                 entries (one per line, '#' comments allowed) whose diff is
--                 expected/acknowledged for this PR and should not fail the
--                 build. See ci/jenkins/expected_regression_diffs.txt.
--
--    _______     ___
-- + 6 @ |||| # P ||| +
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local sql = require "sqlite3"

local LAYERS = { "moments", "vlasov", "gyrokinetic", "pkpm" }

local statusToString = {
   [-4] = "compile_fail", [-3] = "timeout", [-2] = "create", [-1] = "skip",
   [0] = "fail", [1] = "pass",
}
-- Statuses that block a PR build unless explicitly acknowledged.
local BAD_STATUSES = { [0] = true, [-3] = true, [-4] = true }

local resultsDir = GKYL_COMMANDS_L[1]
local ackFile = GKYL_COMMANDS_L[2]

if not resultsDir then
   print("Usage: gkeyll check_regression_results.lua <resultsDir> [ackFile]")
   os.exit(1)
end

-- Parse the acknowledgment file into a set of "<layer>/<name>" entries.
-- Blank lines and '#' comments (including trailing '# reason' text) are
-- ignored.
local acked = {}
if ackFile then
   local f = io.open(ackFile, "r")
   if f then
      for line in f:lines() do
         local entry = line:gsub("#.*$", ""):match("^%s*(.-)%s*$")
         if entry and entry ~= "" then acked[entry] = true end
      end
      f:close()
   end
end

local npass, ackedHits, unacked = 0, {}, {}

for _, layer in ipairs(LAYERS) do
   local dbPath = string.format("%s/%s/regressiondb", resultsDir, layer)
   local f = io.open(dbPath, "r")
   if not f then
      print(string.format("WARNING: no regressiondb for layer '%s' at %s (skipped)", layer, dbPath))
   else
      f:close()
      local conn = sql.open(dbPath)
      local guid = conn:rowexec("select guid from RegressionMeta order by rowid desc limit 1")
      if guid then
         local t, nrow = conn:exec(string.format(
            "select name, status from RegressionData where guid=='%s'", guid))
         for i = 1, nrow do
            local status = tonumber(t.status[i])
            local key = layer .. "/" .. t.name[i]
            if status == 1 then
               npass = npass + 1
            elseif BAD_STATUSES[status] then
               if acked[key] then
                  table.insert(ackedHits, key)
               else
                  table.insert(unacked, { key = key, status = statusToString[status] or tostring(status) })
               end
            end
         end
      end
      conn:close()
   end
end

print(string.format(
   "MOAT results: %d passed, %d acknowledged diff(s), %d unacknowledged failure(s)",
   npass, #ackedHits, #unacked))

if #ackedHits > 0 then
   print(string.format("Acknowledged (per %s):", tostring(ackFile)))
   for _, key in ipairs(ackedHits) do print("  " .. key) end
end

if #unacked > 0 then
   print("")
   print("UNACKNOWLEDGED FAILURES:")
   for _, u in ipairs(unacked) do
      print(string.format("  %s [%s]", u.key, u.status))
   end
   print("")
   print("If any of these are an expected/intentional change (e.g. a physics")
   print("or algorithm change), add a line for each to")
   print("ci/jenkins/expected_regression_diffs.txt with a short reason, e.g.:")
   for _, u in ipairs(unacked) do
      print(string.format("  %s   # <why this changed>", u.key))
   end
   os.exit(1)
end

os.exit(0)

input.new_string:
1. `printenv` — for debugging the build environment.
2. `make clean` and `rm -rf $WORKSPACE/gkylsoft $WORKSPACE/_main_baseline` —
   the workspace persists across builds for a given branch/PR, so without
   this, a stale or (e.g. from a prior interrupted or racing build)
   corrupted file can look up-to-date and never get rebuilt/reinstalled,
   silently breaking the link or mixing old and new dependency files. Wiping
   everything every run makes each build genuinely from scratch.
3. That node's `mkdeps` script (e.g. `machines/mkdeps.macos.sh`) — builds
   `gkylsoft/` from scratch into `$WORKSPACE/gkylsoft`.
4. That node's `configure` script (e.g. `machines/configure.macos.sh`) —
   generates `config.mak` pointing at that freshly-built `gkylsoft/`.
5. `make -j3 check` — builds **and runs** all unit tests (`core`, `moments`,
   `vlasov`, `gyrokinetic`, `pkpm`); a failing unit test fails the build.
6. `make -j3 regression` — builds (does not execute) all regression tests,
   matching today's `.github/workflows/mac_build.yml` scope. This is a cheap
   compile-only smoke check across the full regression-test corpus; it
   doesn't overlap with step 8 below, which actually runs a curated subset.
7. `make -j3 gkeyll-install` — installs the built tree into
   `$WORKSPACE/gkylsoft/gkeyll`, which the regression-test runner (step 8)
   needs: `gkeyll` is both the interpreter it runs as, and its C tests are
   compiled on the fly using the installed `share/Makefile`.
8. **PR builds only** — actually runs the MOAT ("Mother Of All Tests")
   curated regression-test subset (34 tests across `moments`/`vlasov`/
   `gyrokinetic`/`pkpm`) via `gkeyll runregression`, and fails the build on
   any unacknowledged failure or diff:
   1. Builds the PR's target branch (`main`, normally) from scratch in a
      side workspace (`$WORKSPACE/_main_baseline`) and runs
      `gkeyll runregression run --moat create` there, producing a baseline
      generated on this same node/build — never a stale or
      cross-machine-generated one (the default comparison tolerance is
      `1e-12`, tight enough that results aren't guaranteed to reproduce
      bit-for-bit across different machines/toolchains/BLAS builds).
   2. Configures `runregression` for the PR's own install, moves that
      baseline's accepted outputs into the PR's own `gkeyll-results/` tree,
      and runs `gkeyll runregression run --moat check` there, executing the
      34 tests and diffing their output against it.
   3. Runs `ci/jenkins/check_regression_results.lua` against the resulting
      per-layer `regressiondb` files, which fails the build if any test
      didn't pass **unless** it's listed in
      `ci/jenkins/expected_regression_diffs.txt` — see below. `main`-branch
      builds skip this whole stage (there's no target branch to diff
      against) but do a cheap check that this file has been cleared out.

   Building the PR's target branch from scratch roughly doubles a PR
   build's total time; that's the tradeoff for a same-session baseline
   instead of a committed or stale one.
9. Archives `build/**/*.log` and, for the regression-test stage,
   `gkylsoft/gkeyll-results/**/*.txt`/`regressiondb`, so logs and results are
   downloadable from the Jenkins build page even on failure.

### Acknowledging an expected regression diff

If a PR intentionally changes a MOAT test's output (e.g. a physics or
algorithm change), the build's `check_regression_results.lua` step still
fails until you tell it that's expected: add a
`<layer>/<test-name>` line to `ci/jenkins/expected_regression_diffs.txt`
(the failing build's console output prints the exact line to add) with a
short reason, then push again. **Clear those lines back out once the PR is
merged** — an entry left behind could silently hide a real future regression

This all reads correctly and matches the implementation. The implementation is complete:

1. **`ci/jenkins/Jenkinsfile`** — added `Install` stage (`make -j3 gkeyll-install`), a PR-only `Regression baseline (main)` stage that builds the PR's target branch fresh in `_main_baseline/` and runs `runregression run --moat create` there, and a `Regression tests (MOAT)` stage that configures the PR's own `runregression`, `mv`s the baseline's accepted outputs in, runs `--moat check`, and evaluates results via the new checker script. `main`-branch builds instead get a cheap non-blocking check for a stale acknowledgment file. `Clean` and `archiveArtifacts` were extended accordingly.
2. **`ci/jenkins/check_regression_results.lua`** (new) — queries each layer's `regressiondb` (same `sql.open`/schema conventions as `runregression.lua`/`queryrdb.lua`) for non-passing tests, cross-references `expected_regression_diffs.txt`, and exits non-zero on any unacknowledged failure.
3. **`ci/jenkins/expected_regression_diffs.txt`** (new) — the per-PR acknowledgment file, starting empty with usage instructions.
4. **`ci/jenkins/README.md`** — documented the new stages and the acknowledgment-file workflow.

While implementing I verified several load-bearing details directly against the source: `INSTALL_PREFIX ?= ${PREFIX}` (Makefile:50) so no extra flags are needed for `gkeyll-install`; `runregression`'s config file path is derived per-binary from each prefix's own `share/config.mak` (not a single global `~/runregression.config.lua`), so the two parallel `configure` calls (main-baseline and PR) don't clobber each other; and `gkeyll`'s CLI passes extra arguments to scripts via `GKYL_COMMANDS_L`, not a standard Lua `arg` table, which the new checker script uses accordingly.

No tests were run since this all requires a real Jenkins node/build to exercise end-to-end, per the plan's verification section.

A tangential question: on GitHub I see there are two checks, continuous-integration/jenkins/branch and continuous-integration/jenkins/pr-head. Why are there two and what's the difference between them?

Those two checks come from the Jenkins **GitHub Branch Source plugin** (the multibranch pipeline scanner), and they show up because it's indexing the same commit twice — once as a regular branch, once as a pull request:

- **`continuous-integration/jenkins/branch`** — from the "Discover branches" strategy. The scanner treats every branch in the repo (not just `main`) as its own multibranch item and builds/reports on it directly.
- **`continuous-integration/jenkins/pr-head`** — from the "Discover pull requests from origin/forks" strategy, specifically the "head" mode (build the PR branch's tip commit as-is, not merged into the target). This is the item type your `Jenkinsfile`'s `env.CHANGE_ID`/`CHANGE_TARGET` logic is written for.

You get *both* checks on the same PR specifically because your PRs are opened from branches **within the same repo** (not forks) — e.g. `manauref:agent_tools-jenkins` pushed to `gkeyllorg/gkeyll` directly. The branch-discovery strategy sees `agent_tools-jenkins` as a plain branch and builds it under `.../branch`; the PR-discovery strategy sees the *same commit* as the head of a pull request and builds it again under `.../pr-head`. Two multibranch "items," two builds, two GitHub status contexts, same code.

If this double-build is wasted effort (it usually is), the standard fix is in the multibranch job's branch-source config: under **"Discover branches,"** switch the strategy to **"Exclude branches that are also filed as PRs"** (in older plugin versions this is a checkbox; in newer ones it's a strategy dropdown value). That leaves branch-discovery only picking up branches with no open PR, so once you open a PR, only `pr-head` builds/reports on it — `main` itself still gets its own `.../branch` check as before, since it's never a PR head.

    "Discover pull requests from origin". Add "Discover pull requests from
    forks" only if external contributors submit PRs from forks.

    Our PRs are opened from branches within the same repo (not forks), so
    with "All branches" the scanner indexes each such branch twice — once as
    a plain branch, once as a PR head — building it twice and posting two
    separate GitHub status checks for the same commit
    (`continuous-integration/jenkins/branch` and `.../pr-head`). Excluding
    branches that are also filed as PRs leaves `main` (and any other branch
    with no open PR) reporting as `.../branch`, while PR branches report
    only as `.../pr-head`.
